subject: Social Media
title: Emotional Arousal
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Emotional Arousal.

hook.text: Calm articles get read. Angry articles get shared. The difference is arousal—your body's activation.

buildup.text: Berger and Milkman studied 7,000 New York Times articles. High-arousal content shared far more.

discovery.text: Awe, anger, and anxiety all drive sharing. They activate the body. Sadness and calm do not.

twist.text: This means uplifting and infuriating content compete for the same viral slot. Both are high-arousal.

climax.text: Platforms discovered this accidentally. But once they knew, they optimized feeds for arousal.

punchline.text: If it gets your heart racing, you'll share it.

quiz.question: Which emotions drive the most sharing according to research?
